name: Haryana
blurb: Framing the National Capital Region, Haryana's plains hold the legendary battlefield of the Mahabharata and some of India's largest sacred tanks.

districts.name: Kurukshetra
districts.blurb: A pilgrimage town traditionally identified as the battlefield of the Mahabharata war.

places.name: Brahma Sarovar & Jyotisar
places.blurb: One of the largest man-made sacred tanks in India, at the heart of the town traditionally identified as the Mahabharata's battlefield and the site of the Bhagavad Gita's telling.
places.bestPhoto: Ghats reflected in Brahma Sarovar at sunset
places.history: Kurukshetra is traditionally identified as the site of the Mahabharata war and the place where Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita to Arjuna at Jyotisar. Brahma Sarovar itself has been a pilgrimage site for centuries, its ghats rebuilt and expanded across multiple eras, notably in the early 19th century.
places.architecture: Brahma Sarovar is a vast rectangular stepped tank with ghats around its perimeter; Jyotisar features a sacred banyan tree traditionally associated with the Gita's recitation, alongside a modern memorial marking the spot.

timeline.label: Tank renovation and ghat construction expanded under regional patronage.
Kurukshetra Development Board formally established to preserve and develop the pilgrimage circuit.

facts: Brahma Sarovar is one of the largest religious tanks in Asia by surface area.
Kurukshetra hosts a major International Gita Mahotsav festival annually.
The battlefield described in the Mahabharata is traditionally located across this wider region.
hiddenGems: Sannihit Sarovar, a smaller adjoining sacred tank
Sheikh Chmilli's Tomb, a lesser-visited Mughal-era monument nearby
food: Simple Haryanvi thali with bajra khichdi
Lassi from stalls near the tank
experiences: Visiting during the annual Gita Jayanti / Mahotsav
Heritage walk through the Kurukshetra pilgrimage circuit

travel.parking: At Brahma Sarovar and Jyotisar separately
travel.tip: Visit around sunset for the tank's evening aarti, when it is at its most atmospheric.
